title: Farouk El-Baz, 'the king' of Apollo site selection
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Farouk El-Baz, 'the king' of Apollo site selection, about 1960s at NASA, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Farouk El-Baz, who oversaw lunar science planning and helped select Apollo landing sites, was nicknamed the king by the astronauts. His father was a scholar of Egyptian religion.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Farouk El-Baz, a scientist who oversaw lunar science planning for Apollo, NASA's moon landing programme of the 1960s, and helped pick where the astronauts landed, was nicknamed "the king" by the astronauts. Michels adds that El-Baz's father was a scholar of Egyptian religion, and tells it as part of his idea that ancient religious themes ran through the space programme.
